cases.question: What is myopia and how is it corrected?
keyFacts: myopia is also called near-sightedness or short-sightedness
a person with myopia can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects clearly
it is corrected using a concave lens of suitable power

cases.question: Why does the sky appear blue?
keyFacts: sunlight is scattered by the atmosphere
shorter wavelengths (blue) are scattered more than longer wavelengths
this is why the sky appears blue to an observer on Earth

cases.question: What is the Tyndall effect?
keyFacts: the Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles
the path of a beam of light passing through a true solution is not visible, but is visible through a colloidal solution

cases.question: What is dispersion of light and what happens when white light passes through a prism?
keyFacts: dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colours
when white light passes through a glass prism, it splits into a band of colours called a spectrum
the order of colours is VIBGYOR: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red

cases.question: What is the power of accommodation of the human eye?
keyFacts: the ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length is called the power of accommodation
the ciliary muscles adjust the focal length by changing the curvature of the eye lens

cases.question: Why do stars appear to twinkle at night?
keyFacts: stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction of starlight
the apparent position of the star fluctuates slightly due to changing refractive index of the atmosphere
stars are point-sized sources of light, so the fluctuation in their brightness is noticeable

cases.question: What is hypermetropia?
keyFacts: hypermetropia is also called far-sightedness or long-sightedness
a person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects clearly
it is corrected using a convex lens of appropriate power

cases.question: What is the function of the iris in the human eye?
keyFacts: the iris is a dark muscular diaphragm that controls the size of the pupil
it regulates the amount of light entering the eye

cases.question: What is a reflex action? Give an example.
keyFacts: a reflex action is a sudden, involuntary, automatic response to a stimulus
the reflex arc is the pathway: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
examples include pulling the hand away from a hot object or knee-jerk reflex

cases.question: What are the functions of the three main parts of the human brain?
keyFacts: the cerebrum controls voluntary actions, thinking, memory and sensations
the cerebellum controls balance and coordination of voluntary movements
the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions like breathing, heartbeat, and blood pressure

cases.question: What are hormones and how do they differ from nerve impulses?
keyFacts: hormones are chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands directly into the blood
unlike nerve impulses which are fast and targeted, hormonal responses are slower but longer lasting

cases.question: What is the role of auxin in plant movement?
keyFacts: auxin is a plant hormone that promotes cell elongation
when light falls on one side of a plant shoot, auxin diffuses to the shaded side
the cells on the shaded side elongate more, causing the shoot to bend towards light (phototropism)

cases.question: Which gland is called the master gland and why?
keyFacts: the pituitary gland is called the master gland
it controls the secretion of hormones from many other endocrine glands

cases.question: What is a solenoid and what does its magnetic field look like?
keyFacts: a solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder
the magnetic field inside a solenoid is uniform and similar to that of a bar magnet
one end of the solenoid acts as a north pole and the other as a south pole

cases.question: State Fleming's left-hand rule.
keyFacts: stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other
the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field
the middle finger points in the direction of the current
the thumb gives the direction of the force (or motion) on the conductor

cases.question: What is an electric fuse and how does it protect a circuit?
keyFacts: an electric fuse is a safety device that protects circuits from overloading and short-circuiting
it is made of a wire with a low melting point
when excessive current flows, the fuse wire heats up and melts, breaking the circuit

cases.question: What is the right-hand thumb rule?
keyFacts: the right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor
if you wrap your right hand around the conductor with the thumb pointing in the direction of current, the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field

cases.question: What is the difference between a short circuit and an overload?
keyFacts: a short circuit occurs when the live and neutral wires come in direct contact, causing a very large current to flow
an overload occurs when too many appliances are connected to a single circuit, drawing more current than the wiring can safely carry

cases.question: What are magnetic field lines and what are their properties?
keyFacts: magnetic field lines are imaginary lines that represent the direction of the magnetic field
they emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole
no two field lines are found to cross each other
the closeness of field lines indicates the strength of the field

cases.question: What is a tangent to a circle?
keyFacts: a tangent to a circle is a line that intersects the circle at exactly one point
the point where the tangent touches the circle is called the point of contact

cases.question: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
keyFacts: the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact
this is Theorem 10.1 in NCERT
the proof uses the fact that the radius is the shortest distance from the centre to the tangent line

cases.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point?
keyFacts: exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point
the lengths of these two tangents are equal

cases.question: What is a secant of a circle?
keyFacts: a secant is a line that intersects a circle at two points

cases.question: Compare how the nervous system and hormones coordinate body functions differently.
keyFacts: the nervous system uses electrical impulses for fast, precise, short-duration responses
hormones are chemical messengers that travel through the blood and produce slower, longer-lasting, more widespread responses

cases.question: What is the connection between the magnetic field around a solenoid and a bar magnet?
keyFacts: the magnetic field pattern of a solenoid is similar to that of a bar magnet
one end of the solenoid acts as a north pole and the other as a south pole

cases.concept: dispersion of light through a prism
keyFacts: dispersion is the splitting of white light into its component colours
a glass prism produces a spectrum with the colours VIBGYOR
different colours have different wavelengths and are refracted by different amounts

cases.concept: power of accommodation of the human eye
keyFacts: power of accommodation is the ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length
the ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens to focus on near or distant objects

the reflex arc is: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord (relay neuron) → motor neuron → effector

gibberellins promote stem growth
cytokinins promote cell division
abscisic acid inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves

when current flows through a solenoid, it produces a magnetic field similar to a bar magnet

cases.concept: Fleming's left-hand rule for force on a current-carrying conductor
keyFacts: Fleming's left-hand rule determines the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
forefinger = magnetic field direction, middle finger = current direction, thumb = force/motion direction

cases.concept: tangent to a circle and its properties
keyFacts: a tangent touches the circle at exactly one point called the point of contact
the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact
two tangents from an external point are equal in length

cases.question: Can a person with myopia see distant objects clearly?
keyFacts: no, a person with myopia cannot see distant objects clearly
myopia means they can see nearby objects clearly but distant objects appear blurry

cases.question: Do two magnetic field lines ever cross each other?
keyFacts: no, two magnetic field lines never cross or intersect each other
if they did cross, the compass needle would point in two directions at the same point, which is impossible

cases.question: If the ciliary muscles of a person cannot adjust the eye lens for near vision, what defect does the person have and what lens is used to correct it?
keyFacts: the person has hypermetropia (far-sightedness)
a convex lens is used to correct it
